title: De Broglie wavelength and matter waves
topicTitle: De Broglie wavelength and matter waves
notes: De Broglie proposed that matter has a wavelength λ = h / p, where p is the momentum and h is Planck's constant. A faster or heavier particle has a shorter wavelength.
For an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference V, (1/2) m v^2 = e V, so p = √(2 m e V) and λ = h / √(2 m e V).
In angstroms a useful electron form is λ ≈ 12.27 / √V when V is in volts. At 100 V the wavelength is about 1.23 Å, the size of atomic spacings, which is why electron diffraction is visible.
A cricket ball has a tiny wavelength because its momentum is huge. Its wave nature is real and undetectable. The effect shows up for electrons, neutrons and atoms.
Davisson and Germer diffracted electrons from a nickel crystal and found the wavelength that de Broglie predicted. That is the experimental anchor.
The wave is not the electron wiggling through a medium. It is the wave associated with the probability of finding the electron. The electron is still detected as a particle.
